text:
ravi: Heads-up — noticed repeated cudaMalloc spikes on the kv-cache hot path during multi-request bursts. Baseline run attached. nsys shows lots of short-lived allocations around kernel launches, looks like arena churn.

ravi: Command I ran:
```
nsys profile -o kv-cache-spike --trace=cuda,kernels --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi ./bench_kvcache --burst=100
```

mike: can you paste the nsys summary (top kernels / malloc calls)?

ravi: pasted short snippet from nsys report:
```
Time(ms)  Kernel         Calls  Avg(ms)
0.12      kv_lookup      1000   0.0008
0.05      cudaMalloc     400    0.0001
0.20      memcpyHostToDevice 300 0.0006
```
also a kernel timeline snapshot: cudaMalloc events interleaved with kernel launches, many tiny allocations <8KB.

alyssa: did the recent kvcache pooling PR change host vs device alloc path? iirc we switched to hostAlloc fallback for some paths (PR #413).

june: @alyssa yep PR #413 added a host-backed arena for evictions (to avoid device pinned OOMs). config default slab_threshold was 4096 (4KB) so anything <=4KB used the slab allocator, >4KB used cudaMalloc.

mike: quick hypothesis: fragmentation + small-object churn means the slab allocator is frequently freeing and hitting the device allocator for larger ones, causing the observed spikes. also we might be triggering cudaMalloc from threads that previously used pooled buffers.

ravi: i ran an nvprof/gpu-trace for the hot interval: there are ~350 cudaMallocs in a 30s window during bursts, each ~100us but they coincide with kernel scheduling overhead and introduce stalls.

june: can you try raising the pool slab_threshold to 64KB for the eviction path and enable reuse across requests? small change to config: 
```json
{"kvcache": {"eviction_pool_slab_threshold": 65536, "arena_max_frag_ratio": 0.2}}
```

ravi: did an A/B run (same workload) with threshold=64KB. Results: cudaMalloc count down from ~350->~70 in the window, p95 latency for the burst path improved from 220ms -> 160ms. CPU-side scheduling stalls reduced in perfetto timeline.

mike: nice. any increase in memory usage? fragmentation?

ravi: resident GPU memory +8% at peak, average steady-state similar. Arena fragmentation metrics show fewer small free blocks and larger contiguous free chunks.

alyssa: sounds promising. we should be careful — raising slab threshold may keep more GPU memory pinned. need an escape hatch (auto-evict) if GPU goes above soft-limit.

ravi: agreed. I added a config for soft_limit and fallback: if resident > 0.85 * quota, revert slab_threshold to 4KB and trigger compaction. Verified in a synthetic run it falls back correctly.

infra-bot: deploy finished: kvcache-pool-tune -> staging (build 2026.3.5) :rocket:

june: can someone open a perf ticket and record the nvprof/nsys/perfetto links + before/after numbers? tag SRE for rollout guidance.

sre-oncall: opened ENG-672 with attached traces and numbers (nvprof/ perfetto links). assigned to @ravi and @june.

mike: follow-up idea: add a histogram sampler in the runtime to detect allocation size distribution in prod (sample 1/1000 requests) so we can pick thresholds per-customer. low-cost telemetry.

ravi: +1. i'll prototype a non-blocking sampler that emits aggregated size buckets to metrics. if we get stable profiles we can auto-tune slab thresholds per deployment.

alyssa: remember to redact any customer ids in traces before attaching.

ravi: noted. i'll scrub traces and push to ENG-672. thanks all :thumbsup:
